senses.definition: such as to provoke dislike
an inclination to withhold approval from some person or group
a feeling of aversion or antipathy
examples: my dislike of him was instinctive

senses.definition: have or feel a dislike or distaste for
regarded with aversion
move out of position
examples: the artificial hip joint luxated and had to be put back surgically

senses.definition: put out of its usual place, position, or relationship
separated at the joint
an event that results in a displacement or discontinuity
the act of disrupting an established order so it fails to continue
examples: the social dislocations resulting from government policies
his warning came after the breakdown of talks in London

senses.definition: a displacement of a part (especially a bone) from its normal position (as in the shoulder or the vertebral column)
remove or force out from a position
examples: The dentist dislodged the piece of food that had been stuck under my gums
He finally could free the legs of the earthquake victim who was buried in the rubble

senses.definition: change place or direction
remove or force from a position of dwelling previously occupied
examples: The new employee dislodged her by moving into her office space

senses.definition: forced removal from a position of advantage
forced removal from a position of advantage
expressing disapproval
showing lack of love for your country
deserting your allegiance or duty to leader or cause or principle
examples: disloyal aides revealed his indiscretions to the papers

senses.definition: without loyalty; in a disloyal manner
examples: his men acted disloyally and betrayed him in the end

senses.definition: the quality of being disloyal
